text:
Olivia H: Quick heads-up — I ran a 30m perf sweep on canary (scheduler tweak + new kernel-selector heuristics). Observed a small p99 spike on small-request routes around 08:42 UTC. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/continuous-batching/instance?orgId=1&panelId=7

deploy-bot: canary deploy started by Olivia H at 2026-02-14T08:15:23Z (sha: abc123)

Sam J: noted. Any KV-cache miss ratio change? that usually moves p99

Olivia H: Yes — KV miss ratio jumped from 1.2% -> 6.8% for route /v1/generate-small during the window. Trace: https://traces.redwood.dev/trace/0xdeadbeef

Maria R: can you paste the token-level latency breakdown for that route? p50/p95/p99

Olivia H: pasted below (samples aggregated over 5m window around spike):

- route: /v1/generate-small
- tokens-per-request: 8-16
- p50 token latency: 9.4ms
- p95 token latency: 28.7ms
- p99 token latency: 142.3ms
- avg batch size: dropped from 6.2 -> 2.1 during spike

Devin P: that batch collapse + KV miss = big perf hit. Was the scheduler selecting small-kernel path or falling back to generic kernels?

Olivia H: Scheduler log shows a switch to generic kernel at ~08:41:55 for the affected worker pool. Profiling snapshot attached:

perf-bot: profile saved -> s3://perf-artifacts/2026-02-14/canary/kern-snap-08-42.pb

Olivia H: quick PromQL I used to correlate:

```
# batch size histogram for route
sum(rate(runtime_batch_size_bucket{route="/v1/generate-small"}[5m])) by (le)

# kv cache miss ratio
sum(rate(kv_cache_miss_total{pool="canary"}[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total{pool="canary"}[5m]))
```

Maria R: Interesting — average batch size dropped which increases per-token scheduling overhead. Any memory pressure logs? maybe GC/evictions causing KV churn?

Olivia H: Node memory looked stable. We did have a transient eviction event on the cache VM around 08:41:30 due to a temporary process scanning large tensors (see infra logs). That aligns with the miss spike.

Sam J: So two factors: (1) cache eviction -> miss spike; (2) scheduler heuristic fallback -> generic kernel and smaller batches. Combo explains p99.

Devin P: Suggestion: 1) tighten kernel selector thresholds so small falling batches stick to optimized kernel a little longer; 2) add KV cache warmup on retry paths; 3) alert on avg-batch-size < 3 for 2min for critical routes.

Olivia H: Agreed. WIP patches:

```
# scheduler config diff (canary)
- prefer_kernel_threshold: 0.7
+ prefer_kernel_threshold: 0.55  # allow optimized kernel to be chosen under smaller headroom

# alert rule (prometheus)
- alert: LowBatchSize
  expr: avg_over_time(runtime_batch_size{route="/v1/generate-small"}[2m]) < 3
  for: 2m
  labels: {severity: "page"}
```

perf-bot: new canary alert rule applied to canary cluster (id: canary-42)

Maria R: Also add KV eviction metric to the dashboard and tie to per-route regression alert. We should be able to correlate cache evictions -> p99 regressions automatically.

Olivia H: I'll land the selector tweak and the alert, and add the eviction panel. Will monitor canary for 1h and post updates. Plan B is rollback of sched tweak if we see regressions.

Sam J: Thanks. If p99 still >100ms after fixes, let's revert and run a controlled microbenchmark with synthetic tiny prompts.

Devin P: I'll instrument a queue-wait heatmap panel (bucketed by wait ms) so we can see scheduler queuing efficiency.

Olivia H: Perfect. I'll kick off the canary run now.

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed at 2026-02-14T09:03:10Z (sha: abc124)

Olivia H: Update: 15m post-fix: kv miss ratio back to 1.4%, avg batch size stabilized at 5.8, p99 dropped to 48.6ms on that route. Keeping watch for next 45m. :thumbsup: \n
Maria R: Nice! please add a note in the perf run doc and mark the canary as stable if no regression in 1h.

Olivia H: Will do. Thanks all. :rocket:
